title: Minimum Falling Path Sum
spaceBreakdown:
- in-place modification of `matrix`: no extra container → O(1)
- scalar variables (n, i, j, best, ans): O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input matrix
approach: Use dynamic programming in place: for each cell (i, j), the minimum falling-path sum ending there equals matrix[i][j] plus the minimum of the three reachable sums from row i-1 (columns j-1, j, j+1, when valid). Process rows top to bottom; the answer is the minimum value in the last row. Correctness follows from optimal substructure: any optimal path to (i, j) must use an optimal path to one of its three predecessors.
hints: When extending a path from row i to row i+1, what information about row i is actually needed to choose the best predecessor for each cell in row i+1?
Use in-place DP where matrix[i][j] becomes the minimum falling-path sum ending at (i, j). For matrix = [[2,1,3],[6,5,4],[7,8,9]], matrix[1][0] = 6 + min(matrix[0][0], matrix[0][1]) = 6 + 1 = 7.

**Single cell** - n = 1, no falling step exists
`Input: [[5]]` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: initialising `ans = 0` then taking min with last row returns 0 instead of 5

**All negatives** - every cell is negative, so the answer is the most negative path
`Input: [[-1,-2,-3],[-4,-5,-6],[-7,-8,-9]]` → `Expected: -18`
⚠️ Bug: initialising `ans = 0` instead of `matrix[n-1][0]` returns 0 instead of -18

**Boundary column** - first and last columns have only two valid predecessors
`Input: [[1,2],[3,4]]` → `Expected: 4`
⚠️ Bug: reading `matrix[i-1][j-1]` without the `j > 0` guard at j = 0 accesses `matrix[i-1][-1]`, producing undefined/garbage output instead of 4

followUps.q: Reconstruct and return one actual minimum falling path (list of columns chosen per row).
followUps.a: After filling the DP table, start at the argmin of the last row and walk upward: at cell (i, j), pick the predecessor column among j-1, j, j+1 with the smallest DP value, breaking ties arbitrarily. Store columns in a vector and reverse. Time stays O(n²), space O(n) for the path.

followUps.q: Do not modify the input matrix; keep auxiliary space O(n).
followUps.a: Keep only the previous row's DP values in a vector<int> prev of size n, and compute the current row into a vector<int> cur. Each cur[j] = matrix[i][j] + min of prev[j-1], prev[j], prev[j+1] (with bounds checks), then swap prev and cur. Time O(n²), space O(n).

followUps.q: Make the matrix column-circular: column -1 wraps to n-1 and column n wraps to 0.
followUps.a: Same DP, but the predecessor lookup uses modulo: best = min(prev[j], prev[(j-1+n)%n], prev[(j+1)%n]). No bounds checks needed. Time O(n²), space O(1) in-place or O(n) with two rows.
